problem:
Title: Generalized Hilbert Sequence Space is Metric Space/Lemma 1

Let $\alpha$ be an [[Definition:Infinite Cardinal|infinite cardinal number]].

Let $I$ be an [[Definition:Indexed Set|indexed set]] of [[Definition:Cardinality|cardinality]] $\alpha$.

Let $H^\alpha$ be the [[Definition:Generalized Hilbert Sequence Space|generalized Hilbert sequence space of weight $\alpha$]] $\struct{A, d_2}$ where:
:$A$ is the [[Definition:Set|set]] of all [[Definition:Real-Valued Function|real-valued functions]] $x : I \to \R$ such that:
::$(1)\quad \set{i \in I: x_i \ne 0}$ is [[Definition:Countable|countable]]
::$(2)\quad$ the [[Definition:Generalized Sum|generalized sum]] $\ds \sum_{i \mathop \in I} x_i^2$ is a [[Definition:Convergent Net|convergent net]].
:$d_2: A \times A \to \R$ is the [[Definition:Real-Valued Function|real-valued function]] defined as:
::$\ds \forall x = \family {x_i}, y = \family {y_i} \in A: \map {d_2} {x, y} := \paren {\sum_{i \mathop \in I} \paren {x_i- y_i}^2}^{\frac 1 2}$

Let $H = \struct{\ell^2, d_{\ell^2}}$ denote the [[Definition:Hilbert Sequence Space|Hilbert sequence space]], where:
:$\ell^2$ denotes the [[Definition:Real P-Sequence Space|real $2$-sequence space]], that is, the [[Definition:Set|set]] of all [[Definition:Real Sequence|real sequences]] $\sequence {x_n}$ such that the [[Definition:Series of Numbers|series]] $\ds \sum_{n \mathop = 0}^\infty x_n^2$ is [[Definition:Convergent Series of Numbers|convergent]]
:$d_{\ell^2}$ denotes the [[Definition:P-Sequence Metric|real $2$-sequence metric]], that is, the [[Definition:Real-Valued Function|real-valued function]] $d_{\ell^2}: \ell^2 \times \ell^2: \to \R$ defined as:
::$\ds \forall x = \sequence {x_n}, y = \sequence {y_n} \in \ell^2: \map {d_{\ell^2}} {x, y} := \paren {\sum_{n \mathop \ge 0} \paren {x_n - y_n}^2}^{\frac 1 2}$

Let $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_m \in A$.

Then there exists $y_1, y_2, \ldots, y_m \in \ell^2$:
:$\forall a,b \in \closedint 1 m : y_a \ne y_b \iff x_a \ne x_b$
:$\forall a,b \in \closedint 1 m : \map {d_{\ell^2} } {y_a, y_b} = \map {d_2} {x_a, x_b}$
